# doit_extended_metrics (Data Source)

Extended metrics available to the customer: the global extended metrics and the customer's DataHub metrics. The `key` of an item is the `value` of `metric = { type = "extended", value = <key> }` in `doit_custom_metric` variables, reports and alerts. Where a key is accepted depends on its `data_source`: a custom metric variable accepts only `billing` and `billing-datahub` keys (use `filter = "dataSource:billing,billing-datahub"` to list them), and a report or alert accepts the keys of its own data source. A key appears once per data source, so `key` alone is not unique across items. Items are sorted by `label`, then `key`, then `data_source`. Without `max_results` every page is fetched; with it, a single page is returned together with the `page_token` of the next one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    doit = {
      source = "doitintl/doit"
    }
  }
}

# List every extended metric available to the customer. All pages are fetched
# unless max_results is set. A key appears once per data source, so the same
# key can be listed more than once.
data "doit_extended_metrics" "all" {}

output "extended_metric_count" {
  value = data.doit_extended_metrics.all.row_count
}

# A custom metric variable accepts only billing and billing-datahub keys.
data "doit_extended_metrics" "custom_metric_variables" {
  filter = "dataSource:billing,billing-datahub"
}

output "custom_metric_variable_keys" {
  value = [for m in data.doit_extended_metrics.custom_metric_variables.items : m.key]
}

# Look up a key by its label. Use it as the value of
# metric = { type = "extended", value = <key> } in a doit_custom_metric variable,
# a report or an alert.
locals {
  keys_by_label = {
    for m in data.doit_extended_metrics.custom_metric_variables.items : m.label => m.key...
  }
}

output "keys_by_label" {
  value = local.keys_by_label
}

# Read a single page of up to 10 metrics; page_token holds the token of the
# next page. The token is bound to the filter it was returned for.
data "doit_extended_metrics" "first_page" {
  max_results = 10
}

output "next_page_token" {
  value = data.doit_extended_metrics.first_page.page_token
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `filter` (String) Restricts the result by data source, as `dataSource:<value>[,<value>...]`. The only supported key is `dataSource`; its values are `billing`, `billing-datahub`, `bqlens`, `genai-collection`, `kubernetes-utilization` and `tokenomics`. For example `dataSource:billing,billing-datahub` lists the keys a custom metric variable accepts. A `page_token` is bound to the `filter` it was returned for; reusing it with another `filter` fails.
- `max_results` (Number) The maximum number of results to return in a single page. Use the page tokens to iterate through the entire collection.
- `page_token` (String) Page token, returned by a previous call, to request the next page of results
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `row_count` (Number) Optional best-effort total-count hint. Servers include this when
computing it is cheap (indexed count) and MAY return `null` or omit it
for expensive-to-count endpoints. Clients MUST NOT assume this field
is present or non-null. When present, it is the total across all
pages, not just the current page.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `data_source` (String) Data source the metric reads. A custom metric variable accepts `billing` and `billing-datahub` keys. A report or alert accepts the keys of its own `dataSource`. The customer's DataHub metrics are `billing-datahub`.
- `key` (String) Key of the metric. Send it as `value` in `metric: {type: extended, value: <key>}`.
- `label` (String) Name of the metric as the DoiT console shows it.
